questions.stem: What kind of tube is passed into the trachea during rigid bronchoscopy?
questions.answer: A straight metal tube with a bevelled tip

questions.stem: Which rare contraindication to rigid bronchoscopy is a haematological condition?
What patient position is used for rigid bronchoscopy to align the oral, pharyngeal and laryngeal axes?
options: Supine at table edge, neck extended
Prone with the head turned to one side
Sitting upright with the chin tucked

questions.stem: Rigid bronchoscopy ventilation can be given via the side port or by ____.
In rigid bronchoscopy with an open circuit, what is monitored instead of continuous ETCO2?
Which mouth-related complications can follow rigid bronchoscopy?
What airway trauma can rigid bronchoscopy cause?
questions.answer: Tracheobronchial perforation and vocal cord injury

questions.stem: During rigid bronchoscopy, bleeding is especially likely with which manoeuvres?
Why can rigid bronchoscopy cause arrhythmias or haemodynamic instability?
In rigid bronchoscopy, what is the key risk from the underlying airway pathology?
questions.answer: Complete obstruction with inability to ventilate

questions.stem: What airway status in rigid bronchoscopy raises the risk of aspiration?
Why is anaesthesia for rigid bronchoscopy hard to manage?
questions.answer: Very stimulating, yet immobility is needed and coughing must be avoided

questions.stem: What postoperative airway problem should be expected after rigid bronchoscopy?
Which of these is a surgical technique used during rigid bronchoscopy?
Which surgical technique used in rigid bronchoscopy involves a balloon?
What should be assessed preoperatively for rigid bronchoscopy?
Rigid bronchoscopy is usually done for which kind of case and patient?
questions.answer: Urgent or emergency cases in physiologically unwell patients

questions.stem: In rigid bronchoscopy planning, which joint is almost fully extended and must be checked for neck pathology?
Are the ventilation options for rigid bronchoscopy tubed or tubeless, and can they be combined?
questions.answer: All are tubeless and can be combined; the choice depends on patient and procedure

questions.stem: Which tubeless option in rigid bronchoscopy gives oxygen while breathing has stopped?
options: Circle system with a tracheal tube

questions.stem: What does THRIVE rely on for oxygenation during rigid bronchoscopy?
When is manual assistance given during side-port oxygen in rigid bronchoscopy?
Which bronchoscopy-only ventilation option uses positive pressure through the side port?
What advantages does standard circle-system ventilation have in rigid bronchoscopy?
questions.answer: ETCO2 monitoring, volatile delivery possible, most familiar

questions.stem: The Sanders technique is an example of which rigid bronchoscopy ventilation method?
How does jet ventilation deliver gas in rigid bronchoscopy?
questions.answer: High-pressure O2 bursts through a narrow cannula

questions.stem: What are the drawbacks of jet ventilation in rigid bronchoscopy?
questions.answer: Tidal volume and ETCO2 are hard to measure; needs enough expiratory time to avoid gas trapping and barotrauma

questions.stem: Monsoon is an example of which rigid bronchoscopy ventilation method?
What rate range is used in automated high-frequency jet ventilation for rigid bronchoscopy?
In automated high-frequency jet ventilation for rigid bronchoscopy, tidal volumes are smaller than ____.
Which depth of anaesthesia is used to blunt the sympathetic response during rigid bronchoscopy?
Which technique allows precise titration during maintenance for rigid bronchoscopy?
Why is muscle relaxation given during rigid bronchoscopy maintenance?
questions.answer: To prevent coughing or movement against the metal scope, which risks tracheal perforation
